note: Four-year presidential periods 1901-2028. Party: R/D. Control: U=unified (president's party holds both chambers), D=divided, S=split congress (different parties control House and Senate). Assessments are analyst judgments grounded in the indicator datasets; quantitative cells marked '—' where reliable annual data are unavailable (pre-1929 GDP, pre-1948 unemployment, etc.). 'Incomplete' flags current periods. Sources: NBER (recessions), OMB/CBO (debt), BLS/Census/CDC as available.

periods.assessment: Industrial expansion; trust-busting begins; Panic of 1907 still ahead. Debt tiny.
Panic of 1907 exposed unregulated banking; Fed founded 1913 in response. Growth strong overall.
Antitrust enforcement (Standard Oil, American Tobacco); progressive tax movement; GOP splits 1912.
Fed created, income tax, FTC/Clayton; neutrality era of WWI.
WWI mobilization boom; 675k flu deaths; inflation surge; Red Scare and Palmer Raids constrain civil liberties; 19th Amendment.
Sharp 1920-21 deflationary depression (unemployment ~12%) then fast recovery; Mellon tax cuts; Harding scandals; Budget Act 1921.
Roaring Twenties peak: ~4-5% real growth, near-zero inflation, productivity boom; margin-driven stock speculation building.
Worst collapse in US history: GDP -26%, unemployment to ~25%; Smoot-Hawley tariff and tax increase deepened it; gold standard constrained response.
New Deal: banking reform, FDIC, SEC, Social Security; GDP +10.8%/yr avg from Depression floor; unemployment still ~17% by 1936.
Roosevelt recession (fiscal tightening); recovery incomplete; WWII mobilization begins in Europe; US defense build-up 1940.
WWII: GDP +~14%/yr, unemployment to ~1-2%, wage/price controls, rationing; massive debt issuance; internment of Japanese Americans (civil liberties violation); Great Migration accelerates.
Demobilization (-11.6% GDP 1946) then boom; 1946-47 inflation surge; Marshall Plan; Taft-Hartley; debt/GDP falls fast; GI Bill transforms middle class.
Korean War boom; NATO; Cold War institutionalized; inflation subdued; surpluses 1947-49; growth ~4-5%/yr.

periods.control: R Senate, D House (split) 1953-54; D both 1955-56
periods.assessment: Korean War ends; low inflation; highway system; suburban middle-class golden age; 1953-54 recession mild.
1957-58 recession (unemployment 7.1%); Sputnik shock; civil rights tensions (Little Rock); NDEA; low inflation throughout.
Growth accelerates (4.4%+); 1964 tax cut; Civil Rights Act 1964; Kennedy assassination; early Great Society; inflation quiescent.

Peak postwar prosperity: ~5.5%/yr growth, unemployment ~3.5-4%; Medicare/Medicaid, VRA, War on Poverty cuts poverty sharply; Vietnam escalation and Great Society spending begin to overheat; urban riots 1965-68; inflation rising by 1968.

periods.control: D (R Senate 1969-70? no — D controlled both 1969-70? 91st Congress: D both chambers; 92nd (1971-72): D both)
periods.assessment: Mild recession 1970; wage-price controls Aug 1971; Bretton Woods collapse; détente; EPA/OSHA/Title IX; inflation suppressed then brewing.
Worst recession since 1930s (until 2008): unemployment 9% (1975), inflation 12% (1974); controls' pent-up inflation unleashed; Watergate; resignation; NYC fiscal crisis.
Stagflation peaks: CPI 13.5% (1980), prime 20%; deregulation of airlines/trucking; Volcker appointed 1979; unemployment ends where it began (~7.5%).
Volcker disinflation completes: inflation 13.5%→4%; 1981-82 recession (10.8% unemployment) then boom (7.2% 1984); ERTA tax cut; deficits explode (debt/GDP 26%→34%); S&L deregulation.
Growth ~3.5-4.2%/yr; TRA 1986 tax reform; Black Monday crash recovered within 2 years; S&L losses building; Iran-Contra; unemployment to 5.4%.
1990-91 recession (oil shock, credit crunch from S&L cleanup); 1990 deficit deal (tax increase); Cold War ends; unemployment rises 5.4%→7.3%; defeat in 1992.
Deficit reduction act 1993; NAFTA; welfare reform 1996; growth accelerates; unemployment 7.3%→5.4%; inflation ~2.8%; bond-market rout 1994.
Tech boom peak: growth 4.1-4.7%, unemployment to 3.9-4.0%, surpluses 1998-2000, debt/GDP falls to ~32.5%; dot-com bubble inflates; GLB 1999.
Recession and 9/11 shock; two wars; 2001/2003 tax cuts; housing boom begins (low rates); deficits return; S&P down for the period.
Housing bubble peaks 2006, collapses 2007-08; worst financial crisis since 1929; TARP; unemployment begins surge (7.8% by Jan 2009); debt/GDP 36%→53%.
Crisis response: ARRA, TARP completion, auto rescue, ACA, Dodd-Frank; recovery slow but steady; deficit 9.8%→6.8%; unemployment 10%→7.9%.
Sequestration/austerity; growth ~2.1-3.1%; unemployment 7.9%→4.7%; deficits to 3.2%; fracking boom; ACA exchanges live; stock market to records.
TCJA; 2.7%/yr growth 2017-19; record-low unemployment 3.5% (Feb 2020); COVID: sharpest-but-shortest recession; CARES $2.2T; debt/GDP 77%→100%; Jan 6, 2021 at period end.

Fastest recovery on record; unemployment 3.4-4.0%; inflation spike 9.1% peak → 2.9%; IRA/CHIPS/Infrastructure; deficits 12.4%→6.4%; real wages rose fastest at bottom; life expectancy recovered; immigration surge; housing unaffordability worsens.

INCOMPLETE. Observed through Aug 2026: GDP +2.1% (2025), slowing into 2026 (Q2 +1.5%); unemployment 4.1-4.5%; inflation ~2.8-3% sticky; deficit ~6% GDP; OBBBA (+$3.4T CBO); tariffs and regulatory rollback; democracy indices at record lows (V-Dem 0.57, FH 81, EIU 7.65); CAPE ~41; debt/GDP ~100% heading to 120% (2036, CBO). No verdicts yet — period incomplete.
